name: Positive Overlaps Survive Rooted Minor Minimization
statement: The following are equivalent: (i) some rooted factor has a degree-two corner root and, after possibly exchanging the root directions, one canonical side/opposite overlap peels to zero; (ii) some ample canonical degree-two presentation is ordinarily peelable, does not peel to its singleton root, has both new-coordinate contractions peeling to the root image, and has that overlap peeling to zero. Every presentation in (ii) has a rooted-factor minor obtained using only old-coordinate operations; its marked root remains a degree-two corner and the corresponding overlap remains root-positive. No old-coordinate minor tests are needed in (ii).
proof: The forward implication follows from the canonical section presentation of a rooted factor. Conversely, positive contractions force both side sections to peel to zero, so all four new-coordinate rooted images are positive. Commuting operations shows that every rooted minor using a new coordinate is positive; hence any root-negative minor retains both new coordinates. Repeatedly take root-negative elementary old-coordinate images until minimal. Ordinary peelability survives, so the terminal image is a rooted factor. Old-coordinate operations preserve the singleton root section and its two incident directions. They also preserve the identity between the image of the overlap and the intersection of the image sections: a new contraction intersection would create opposite square vertices without either intermediate vertex, contradicting isometry. Endpoint minor closure preserves root positivity of the overlap.
